Clara, Tom — thanks for the clear list. High level answers below; I include our infra owners (Monica, Soojin, Marcus) for technical details and attachment of a retention matrix. We can follow up on a call if helpful.

Summary (high level):
- API request logs: metadata (timestamps, request id, model id, latency) retained by default for 365 days in hot store; full request/response bodies (prompt text) are retained by default for 30 days for hosted accounts and used for abuse/quality signals. For Dedicated/Private deployments, prompt storage is configurable and can be disabled per contract.

- Access & audit logs: admin console and IAM audit trails retained 365 days in primary logging cluster; exported audit snapshots available on request.

- Backups / snapshots: automated model-serving state and object-store snapshots are kept for 180 days by default (daily snapshots with a 180-day retention policy). We offer optional archival to cold storage for up to 24 months for customers with regulated needs (on request and noted in DPA amendment).

- Deletion requests & evidence: standard deletion path removes data from the hot store within 72 hours and from searchable indices within 7 days. Snapshots are deleted according to object-store lifecycle (purge job within 14 days of snapshot deletion request) and then subject to irrecoverable overwrite/crypto-delete processes; we can provide a deletion certificate (time-stamped manifest) for provable removal for contractual commitments.

I attached: redwood_log_retention_matrix.csv (matrix with artifact -> store -> retention), SOC2-report-redacted.pdf (redacted), and a draft DPA amendment (DPA_amendment_v1.docx) that outlines options for archival windows and deletion SLAs.

Action items:
1) Please confirm if MediSys requires archival beyond the default 180 days (e.g., 24 months) and whether you need an on-demand purge clause.
2) If you want a deletion certificate for the initial purge, we can draft a template and provide timelines.

- Aditya

Aditya — adding technical clarifications for the retention matrix and deletion runbook that Clara asked for:

- Log types: we separate (a) request logs (per-API invocation, optional payload capture), (b) audit logs (RBAC/console actions), and (c) infra/system logs (node/OS level). Request logs with payloads live in encrypted object store; metadata in time-series DB.

- Prompt retention: hosted accounts have a 30-day default TTL for prompt payloads used for diagnostics/abuse detection. After TTL expiry, objects are marked for deletion and removed from index; underlying object-store lifecycle will perform a least-privilege purge and eventually remove data blocks. For customers that require no prompt retention, we can enable 'no-store' at the tenant level (Private/Dedicated or via contract flag).

- Snapshot deletion runbook:
   1) Customer requests deletion -> ticket created (SOP-ID: RB-DEL-2027-02)
   2) Snapshot removed from primary retention set; lifecycle rule triggered to remove archive copy (if present)
   3) Background purge job performs zeroization/crypto-delete; we log operation id and checksums
   4) Ops attaches deletion manifest and timestamp for customer review

- Chain of custody & evidence: manifests include snapshot id, creation timestamp, deletion timestamp, storage region, and admin operator ID. We can export manifests as signed PDFs for DPO consumption.

If you want, Marcus can prepare a one-off purge test run to demonstrate the flow (non-production snapshot).

—Monica
